notes: The schematic image was not readable, so the wiring is inferred from the sketch: pin 5 drives the white LED (meeting room), pins 2/4/3 drive the RGB LED's R/G/B (lounge area).
I assumed one 220 ohm resistor per LED channel (4 in total). The exact breadboard columns and rows are my own choice.

The MKR ENV Shield is not in the catalogue, so I added it as a new part type. It stacks on the MKR WiFi 1010 and passes pins 2-5 and GND through to its top headers, and the jumper wires attach to those top headers.

Fix for the validator errors: the MKR WiFi 1010's pins are header-pins, so the shield's underside ports (2, 3, 4, 5, GND) are now header-sockets. That makes the stacking joins header-pin to header-socket, which is a compatible pair. Physically the shield's pins plug into the board, but the catalogue's kind rules take priority here.
The MKR ENV Shield's I2C sensors use the board's own bus, so no external wiring is added for the temperature sensor.
The RGB LED has a common cathode, so COM goes to the breadboard's negative rail, which is connected to the board's GND.
The Arduino Cloud and Alexa steps are software only and add no parts or connections.
The board is powered over USB, which is not drawn.
